name: 16f nf4 block quantization
title: NF4 quantization of a block of 8 weights
subtitle: Weights 0.012, -0.031, 0.004, 0.027, -0.008, 0.045, -0.019, 0.002; 16 NF4 levels from the QLoRA paper

steps.caption: The block has 8 weights. Its largest magnitude, 0.045, becomes the block scale, the one number stored at full precision.
Dividing by 0.045 puts every weight between -1 and 1, with the largest one landing exactly on 1.
Each value snaps to the nearest of the 16 NF4 levels, which crowd near zero where most weights lie. Only the 4-bit index of the level is stored.
Multiplying the levels back by 0.045 recovers the weights with a mean error of 0.00081 and a largest error of 0.0017, on the weight 0.027.
A uniform 4-bit grid with levels at multiples of 1/7 does worse on the same block: mean error 0.0012 and largest error 0.0024, because its levels are spread evenly.
A block of 8 pays 4 extra bits per weight for its 32-bit scale. Blocks of 64 pay 0.5, double quantization cuts that to 0.127, and MXFP4 pays 0.25 with an 8-bit scale per 32 weights.
